chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a maid-servant with a stipulation (of return/choice) from a man for a day or two days, so she died while with him, and the price had been paid. Upon whom would the responsibility (for the price) be? He said: There is no responsibility upon the one who bought until he completes his stipulated period.
ai.seo_question: Who bears the risk of loss if a purchased slave dies before the stipulated return period expires?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of khiyar al-shart (option of stipulation), establishing that the buyer bears no risk of loss (daman) for the slave until the agreed-upon inspection period elapses. It underscores the Shia juristic view that ownership transfer is conditional upon the completion of the stipulated term, protecting the buyer from liability for accidental death during this interim. This ruling highlights the importance of contractual clarity in commercial transactions within Islamic law.
